chunks: A shaykh from our companions, called ʿAbdullāh ibn Razīn, narrated to me; he said:

I was residing in al-Madīnah, the city of the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) used to come every day at midday to the mosque. He would dismount in the courtyard, go to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), offer salām to him, then return to the house of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), remove his sandals, stand, and perform salat (prayer).

Then Shayṭān whispered to me and said: “When he dismounts, go and take some of the dust that he treads upon.” So on that day I sat waiting for him in order to do this. When midday came, he (عليه السلام) approached riding his donkey, but he did not dismount in the place where he used to dismount; rather, he came and dismounted upon the rock that was at the door of the mosque. Then he entered and offered salām to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).

He said: Then he returned to the place where he used to perform salat (prayer), and he did this for several days. So I said: “When he removes his sandals, I will come and take the pebbles that his feet tread upon.” But when the next day came, he arrived at midday, dismounted upon the rock, then entered and offered salām to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). Then he came to the place where he used to perform salat (prayer), but he prayed wearing his sandals and did not remove them, and he continued doing that for several days.

So I said to myself: “This did not become possible for me here, but I will go to the door of the bathhouse, and when he enters the bathhouse, I will take some of the dust that he treads upon.” So I asked about the bathhouse that he entered, and it was said to me: “He enters a bathhouse in al-Baqīʿ belonging to a man from the descendants of Ṭalḥah.” I learned the day on which he entered the bathhouse, then went to its door and sat beside the Ṭalḥī, speaking with him while awaiting his coming (عليه السلام). The Ṭalḥī said: “If you want to enter the bathhouse, then get up and enter, for that will not be possible for you after an hour.” I said: “Why?” He said: “Because the son of al-Riḍā intends to enter the bathhouse.”

He said: I said: “And who is the son of al-Riḍā?” He said: “A man from the family of Muḥammad who possesses righteousness and waraʿ.” I said to him: “And is it not permissible that anyone else enter the bathhouse with him?” He said: “We vacate the bathhouse for him when he comes.”

He said: While I was in that state, he (عليه السلام) approached, and with him were some of his servants, and before him was a غلام carrying a mat, until he brought it into the undressing area and spread it out. Then he arrived, offered salām, entered the chamber upon his donkey, entered the undressing area, and dismounted upon the mat. So I said to the Ṭalḥī: “Is this the one whom you described as having righteousness and waraʿ?” He said: “O man, no, by Allah, he has never done this at all except on this very day.” So I said to myself: “This is from my own doing; I brought this about.”

Then I said: “I will wait for him until he comes out; perhaps I may obtain what I wanted when he exits.” But when he came out and dressed himself, he called for the donkey, and it was brought into the undressing area. He mounted from upon the mat and departed (عليه السلام). So I said to myself: “By Allah, I have caused him discomfort, and I will never return to this, nor will I seek again what I had sought from him.” And my resolve upon that became firm.

Then, when midday came on that day, he approached on his donkey until he dismounted in the place where he used to dismount in the courtyard. He entered, offered salām to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), came to the place where he used to perform salat (prayer) in the house of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), removed his sandals, and stood performing salat (prayer).

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday, the time when the sun declines from its zenith
key_terms.الصَّحْنِ: the courtyard area of the mosque
key_terms.بَيْتِ فَاطِمَةَ: the house of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), a sacred location adjacent to the mosque
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: scrupulous piety and cautious avoidance of improper matters
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: offers salām in greeting and reverence

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the awareness, piety, and daily worship of Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This report narrates the daily practice of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) in al-Madīnah and how a man, moved by a whisper of Shayṭān, attempted to obtain traces from where the Imam had walked. The Imam (عليه السلام) perceived this and altered his practice in ways that prevented it, until the man realized he had caused discomfort and repented of his intention. The narration highlights the Imam’s awareness, dignity, devotion in salat (prayer), and the narrator’s eventual moral correction.
